AirTag is a great tool for protecting and tracking luggage, but attaching one to smaller devices like cameras isn't so straightforward.

Some people put an AirTag in a regular protective case and clip it to a camera strap, but that's not exactly discreet — a thief could easily spot it and remove it right away. Fortunately, there are more covert options on the market…

Apple has always stressed that the main use of AirTag is not for theft prevention. Because of its built-in anti-stalking features, a thief will eventually get notified that an AirTag is present. But before that notification pops up, you still have several hours to track your belongings, so plenty of people do use them for anti-theft purposes.

Of course, if a thief spots the AirTag quickly and throws it away, that tracking window becomes pointless. That's why ordinary protective cases, while cheap and easy to attach, can be too easily noticed by thieves.

Fortunately, there are more discreet ways to attach an AirTag to a DSLR or mirrorless camera.

Camera strap attachment

The most basic approach is using a camera strap attachment. These accessories are designed to look like part of the camera strap, and if you use a black strap — especially a thicker, comfort-style one — it blends in even better.

Quick-release plates

Photographers often leave a tripod quick-release plate mounted on the camera permanently for quick mounting and unmounting throughout the day. You can buy quick-release plates with a built-in AirTag slot — these designs are harder to spot.

Tripod adapters

If you can't find a quick-release plate compatible with your tripod, there's another option — a universal adapter.

Camera cages

If you use a camera cage to mount accessories, you can pick a model with a built-in hidden AirTag compartment, or get a standalone AirTag holder that comes with a cage-mounting attachment. The latter may not look especially discreet on its own, but mounted on a cage full of accessories, it won't stand out.

L-brackets

The newest accessory on the scene is Peak Design's Field Bracket. This L-bracket lets you mount the camera on a tripod in either landscape or portrait orientation, and offers optional expansion features like a hand strap and cheese plate for building out your rig. Instead of taking an AirTag, it has a built-in tracker compatible with Find My.

Have you tried any of these methods, or come up with your own? Share your thoughts in the comments.
